example.title: Hylton 1983 C3X cooled vane
example.source: Hylton, Mihelc, Turner, Nealy and York (1983), NASA CR-168015: the C3X radially cooled vane cascade, run 158 (Appendix A), Tables III, IV, IX, Fig. 7.
example.reproduced: Ambient humid air, compressed, burns CH4 so that the cascade inlet is at the measured Tt1 and Pt1 (as in the rig's natural-gas burner). Each row is one stretch of vane surface and the cooling hole nearest to it: burner gas from the cascade inlet to the measured local static pressure, a ss310 wall as thick as the mean distance to the hole, and the hole's share of its coolant flow. The gas-side Nu multipliers are fitted to the measured midspan wall temperature.
example.where_to_look: Solve, then select a wall edge: T_hot is the gas-side wall temperature, equal to the measured Tw of that segment (the tuning target). The gas channels' Nu_multiplier is the fitted tuner (0.7-1.1 mid-chord suction side, about 1.9-2.0 at the leading edge, where a channel correlation has no stagnation flow). Each wall has its two faces: the segment's area on the gas side, the hole's share of its perimeter on the coolant side.
example.label: tuned
example.label_note: Tuned to run 158 (19 Nu multipliers for 19 measured Tw; none left over). Untuned, the smooth-channel network misses run 158 by MAE 24 K (bias -14 K, worst -73 K at the leading edge): cross-source. Run 149 (Tu 6.5% vs 8.3%) with these multipliers: MAE 10 K, bias +9 K. The report's h is inferred by its own FE model, not measured, and is not a target.
